ghost_court.name: Ghost Court
ghost_court.description: A 5.38 m rank in which the four QFEP benches - the theoretical core of this project - stand together for the first time, each rebuilt at full size by its own arithmetic and in its own palette, and the question put to all four at once is what else is allowed to stand beside them. Bay A is f_order_bench's caged crystal with its F meter; bay B is lambda_dial_bench's vertical clock and the field that reads it; bay C is phi_rate_bench's floating column over its emitter ring; bay D is qfep_reactor_bench's console, glass chamber and three horizontal deck dials. Nothing is normalised onto a shared rail: there is no rack, no slat and no bar chart, and a viewer recognises each instrument before reading a single label. The first axis is the companion vocabulary all four benches declare character for character - none, ghost, supply, redaction, quorum - a monotone ladder in which the absent term goes from unrecorded, to an unfitted grey socket, to a lit conduit feeding the phenomenon, to a name struck under a black bar, to an instrumented dial wired into the hub. The second axis is the word the family does NOT share. qfep_reactor_bench returns FROZEN / ALIVE / NOISE; lambda_dial_bench prints FROZEN / LIFE / NOISE; phi_rate_bench prints only FROZEN = DEAD and MOVING = ALIVE and has no third state at all, so bay C builds identically at alive and at noise; and f_order_bench prints no state word anywhere in its file. So reading the rank left to right at verdict = frozen shows one bench celebrating its stated goal - F driven to 0.05, the meter down to a three-pixel stub - beside three benches in the pose their own code calls death.
dev_themes: a shared word for absence and no shared word for life
ghost is hardware for a party who never arrived
the bench that celebrates the pose the others call death
interactions: read the rank left to right at complement = none and find four instruments that record nothing of the terms they dropped - not one glyph anywhere in the frame, which is the value, drawn
walk to ghost and count eight grey sockets: capped stubs, blanked face plates, dead glyphs, nothing lit and nothing connected - provision made and never fitted
walk to supply and watch the same eight positions light up and plug into each bay's hub; walk to quorum and watch them stand up as instrumented dials wired back in
stop at redaction and read what each bench prints about its own cut - and notice the struck terms were never set in the first place, so the bars redact blank bone
hold complement still and sweep verdict: bay C is the same picture at alive and at noise, because phi_rate_bench has nowhere else to go
ghost_court.capacity: SEE that four independently written instruments can agree word for word about how to name what is missing and share no language at all for whether the thing on the bench is alive. The complement ladder is monotone and every step makes the absent term more present and more powered - none (not acknowledged), ghost (acknowledged as unfitted hardware), supply (acknowledged and fed), redaction (acknowledged in writing and struck), quorum (acknowledged, instrumented and wired in) - and all four benches climb it identically because `ghost` is literally one object bolted to four different machines. SEE ALSO where that agreement stops. The verdict axis is the reactor's own triple and it does not fit the family: one bench has no third state, one uses a different word for the middle, and one names no state at all. The contradiction is invisible in any single tile and unmissable in a rank of four.
ghost_court.qfep_connection: F is the shared token: five strings, spelled identically in four separately authored @export_enum lines, matched by four `match complement` statements that all end in a bare `pass`. E is the difference the token hides - each bench isolates a different term of QFE = F - lambdaE(S) + phiDeltaE(S,t), so the same word `ghost` points at lambda and phi in bay A, at F and phi in bay B, at F and lambda in bay C, and at E and S in bay D. Three bays ghost each other; the fourth ghosts the referent, which is why its pair is amber and rose and not a term colour. lambda is what the shared word costs: the same five-value ladder buys three benches a term of the equation and buys the reactor the SYSTEM the terms are terms of, and the reactor's own scalar cannot tell the two apart - at s = 0 it prints QFE = 1.00 and at s = 0.5 it prints QFE = 1.00, a dead lattice and the living edge on the same readout, separated only by a word. The dark spot is the MUTENESS. R7: every billboard title, subtitle and readout of all four benches is omitted, because LabelFramer builds a bezel and a panel behind each one at spawn and four of those would out-mass the phenomena. So the court shows no bench name and no verdict word; the state is read off each source's own meter, needle and colour. What is foreclosed is the reader's ability to check the court against the benches' own captions - and with it the whole verbal layer where the disagreement is actually written. What is bought is the only reading a still permits: four machines in one frame, in their own bodies, differing.
ghost_court.relationships:
Synthesised out of the four scenes that declare a `complement` axis, all four registered in commons/artifacts/registry/qfep.json: [[f_order_bench]] (commons/artifacts/f_order_bench/f_order_bench.gd), [[lambda_dial_bench]], [[phi_rate_bench]] and [[qfep_reactor_bench]]. Verified this pass by parsing all 108 registry files: those are the only four tokens in the corpus declaring `complement`, and all four declare the same five values in the same order.

CONSTRUCTION DELIBERATELY NOT BORROWED FROM [[pressure_yard]] OR [[ladder_hall]]. Both reduced their families to an order-statistic rack - identical slats on grey pads - and pressure_yard recorded the fault in its own registry before ladder_hall repeated it. This court carries each bay's SOURCE GEOMETRY at 1:1, in the source palette, built by the source arithmetic, out of the same `embodied_prop` primitives the four benches are built from. The nearest right-shaped kin are [[tier_terrarium]] (organisms in bays) and [[boundary_tank]] (four actual standing waves).

THE WAVE PAIRING. This is one of two families in the corpus that independently coined BOTH `ghost` and `none`; the other is the `account` axis on [[x_translation_cube]], [[y_translation_cube]], [[z_translation_cube]] and [[axis_translation_cube]] (commons/artifacts/axis_translation_cube/axis_translation_cube.gd:80-95), whose synthesis is [[passage_ledger]]. See dna.kin for what the two words mean here, stated so they can be compared word for word.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: THE YAW IS THE FOOTPRINT, AND IT IS A CHOICE THE MAP CAN UNMAKE. At the shipped `court_yaw` of 0.62 rad the rank stands diagonal to the cell grid and its world AABB is 5.113 x 4.065 m - six cells by five - even though the deck it stands on is 5.540 x 1.040 m, which is six cells by two. The 0.62 buys the thing every pixel claim in this entry depends on: court-local x becomes screen-x exactly (r . dir = cos0.62 sin0.62 - sin0.62 cos0.62 = 0), so all four bays sit at ONE camera depth and each bay's front faces the standpoint square. `court_yaw = 0.0` recovers the 6 x 2 footprint and stands the rank square to a room, and every pixel number in dna.framing_why and dna.still_note then holds only approximately. front 4 because a 5.4 m rank of four separate instruments wants the reader far enough back to hold all four at once; back 0 because everything both axes draw faces the approach and the deepest tenant is bay D's readout panel at bay-local z -0.130. HEIGHT IS 2.66 m, three cells, and it is set by ONE bay: bay C's column floats at y 1.65..2.59 while the other three top out at 1.25, 1.30 and 1.33. A ceiling at 2 decapitates the phi bench, which is the bay carrying the court's sharpest finding (see dna.still_note R6).

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry - every mesh ghost_court.gd's _build would create was enumerated in an independent Python replica at all 15 variants and unioned, counting MeshInstance3D only (capture_config_sweep.gd:1465-1481 counts MultiMeshInstance3D only when there is no MeshInstance3D content at all, and this artifact has no MultiMesh; Label3D never counts). Bay-local extents are all set by the deck, which is the widest and deepest single mesh: 5.5396 x 0.07 x 1.04 at y -0.070..0.000, from _deck_w = court_w + 0.16 and court_w = 5.3796 at court_seed 20260814. After the 0.62 rad yaw its world half-extents are 2.7698*cos(0.62) + 0.52*sin(0.62) = 2.5564 in x and 2.7698*sin(0.62) + 0.52*cos(0.62) = 2.0326 in z, so x = 5.1129 and z = 4.0651. y runs -0.070 (deck underside) to 2.5917 (bay C's topmost sphere, 2.5617 centre + 0.03 radius), = 2.6617. Diagonal 7.05344, radius 3.52672. IDENTICAL AT ALL 15 VARIANTS: the deck sets x and z on its own and bay C's column sets y at both `alive` and `noise`, so neither axis can move the box and capture_config_sweep's union pre-pass and its per-variant fallback give the same camera. Re-measure when a Godot pass is run.

dna.default:
complement=none, verdict=alive.

BOTH ARE THE CODE'S OWN @export DEFAULTS, read off ghost_court.gd:383 and :386 and not chosen here. dna.placements is 0 - verified this pass, no map_data.json and no JSON anywhere under commons/ names this token - so the defaults had only to be the strongest openings.

complement=none AGREES WITH ALL FOUR SOURCES, which is the opposite of the divergence ladder_hall had to declare. f_order_bench.gd:51, lambda_dial_bench.gd:50, phi_rate_bench.gd:55 and qfep_reactor_bench.gd:61 each default `complement` to "none", and following them is the coherent choice for an artifact whose whole claim is that the four speak one vocabulary. It also opens on the honest baseline: `none` is not a blank tile - all four bodies, all four plinths and the deck are present and 31.7% of the crop is lit - it is the four instruments standing exactly as they ship, recording nothing of the terms they dropped. The ladder only means something measured against that.

verdict=alive because it is the only value at which all four bays are in a characteristic and distinguishable state: bay A half-gathered between scatter and lattice, bay B's needle inside the gold band at lambda = 0.4, bay C's column fully extended, bay D's particles at peak aliveness. `frozen` collapses bay C to a 25 x 27 px pile and shortens the whole subject box by 99 rows; `noise` is where bay B overflows its plinth. Neither is a wrong picture but neither is an introduction.
dna.was: nothing. This token did not exist before this pass, and neither did the arrangement. Measured, not assumed: a sweep of all 108 registry files returns exactly four entries declaring a `complement` axis - f_order_bench, lambda_dial_bench, phi_rate_bench and qfep_reactor_bench, all four in qfep.json - and all four declare [none, ghost, supply, redaction, quorum]. None of the four has ever appeared in a frame with any other, so the question of whether one vocabulary means one position could not be put. All four carry a `dna` block containing `axes` and nothing else.
dna.note:
WHAT THE FOUR BENCHES ACTUALLY DECLARE, read out of the code for this entry rather than transcribed (LAW 2).

ALL FOUR USE A REAL @export_enum, unlike the `ladder` family, so tools/check_dna_declarations.py has an engine hint_string to read in every case:

  f_order_bench.gd:51        @export_enum("none", "ghost", "supply", "redaction", "quorum") var complement: String = "none"
  lambda_dial_bench.gd:50    the same line
  phi_rate_bench.gd:55       the same line
  qfep_reactor_bench.gd:61   the same line

each with an identical `const COMPLEMENTS: PackedStringArray` on the next line and apply_grid_config gating on COMPLEMENTS.has(...). ghost_court.gd:383 and :386 are the same form, and gd:543-573 reads the hint string BACK OUT of get_property_list() for both axes and compares it to the const in both directions AND in order, pushing an error on any mismatch - the science_screen gate, built in.

WHERE THE FAMILY AGREES, and it agrees more completely than any family measured so far. `_comp_ghost_one` is byte-identical in all four files apart from the anchor constants (f_order:277-284, lambda_dial:305-317, phi_rate:278-289, reactor:334-349): same materials, same five meshes, same offsets, same font size, even the same comment. `ghost` is one object bolted to four different machines.

WHERE IT DISAGREES, and it is more than the source comments claim:

  1. FOUR CONSTANTS DIFFER, NOT THREE. phi_rate_bench.gd:72 sets COMP_X = 0.34 where the other three set 0.40; qfep_reactor_bench.gd:80-81 sets COMP_Y = 0.615 and COMP_Z = 0.0 where the other three set 0.145 and 0.10.
  2. TWO BUILDERS DIFFER, NOT ONE. The reactor's SUPPLY intake collar is a torus of radius 0.26 tube 0.022 ringing the glass at the point of entry, where the other three use a hidden 0.09 / 0.02 disc; and its REDACTION plate is a different function entirely - two inks, two lit underlines, two bars over EMPTY positions and no mounting strut - against the three-slot _comp_formula_plate(keep) the other three share. So `ghost` is one object built four times, and `supply` and `redaction` are not.
  3. THE VERDICT WORDS ARE NOT SHARED AT ALL, and this is the axis this synthesis exists to put. qfep_reactor_bench._verdict_state() (:233-238) returns exactly "FROZEN" / "NOISE" / "ALIVE" on thresholds 0.28 and 0.72. lambda_dial_bench (:264-271) prints FROZEN / LIFE / NOISE. phi_rate_bench (:242, :245) prints only "FROZEN = DEAD" and "MOVING = ALIVE" - two states, and its `_rate` is clamped to [0.04, 1.0] with _apply_form lerping ONE dead pose to ONE alive pose, so there is no third state and no noise colour. f_order_bench prints NO state word at any value: grep for FROZEN, ALIVE, NOISE, LIFE and DEAD across the whole file returns nothing, its readout is "F down %.2f" (:237) and the word its own truth line uses, "a perfect, frozen, dead thing", never reaches the furniture.

CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD, ALL SEVEN MEASURED IN AN INDEPENDENT PYTHON REPLICA (LAW 2: the code wins, including over the artifact's own header).

  C-A. THE HEADER'S dna.framing OF 0.39 IS WRONG AND IS THE ONE NUMBER IN IT THAT IS. gd:236-250 solves framing from "world union after the yaw is 5.61 x 2.66 x 4.76 m, diagonal 7.83, R = 3.913". The geometry the file actually builds unions to 5.1129 x 2.6617 x 4.0651, diagonal 7.05344, R = 3.52672. Those cannot both be true of the same deck: the deck is the only tenant that sets x or z, and 5.5396 x 1.040 yawed 0.62 gives 5.1129 x 4.0651 by arithmetic the header itself supplies. At framing 0.39 the camera sits at 8.548 m and the court projects to 822.7 px in a 760 px frame - IT CLIPS AT BOTH EDGES, and the rendered subject bbox comes back frame-clamped at x = 0..760, which would also corrupt the critic's crop. EVERY OTHER NUMBER IN THAT HEADER REPRODUCES EXACTLY AT framing 0.44, which is why the correction is a typo and not a redesign: see dna.framing_why for the eight of them.
  C-B. THE HEADER'S BODY COUNT OF 187 MeshInstance3D IS STALE. Measured: 259 at complement=none (1 deck + 82 + 68 + 66 + 42) and 299 at quorum. Its own R8 figure - "299 meshes + 8 Label3D = 307 nodes" - reproduces to the node. Two counts in one docstring, one right.
  C-C. THE Z-STACK OMITS THE GHOST COLLAR. The collar is a TorusMesh, which lies in the XZ plane, radius 0.075 tube 0.016 at y COMP_Y + 0.30, so it spans z 0.009..0.191 and y 0.429..0.461. Its front arc therefore stands 65 mm PROUD of the blanked face plate (0.106..0.126) and crosses the backing plate's bottom 31 mm - about 4 px. No mark is hidden (the glyph ink plane is at y 0.565) but the interval belongs in the stack, and the header lists only the post.
  C-D. THE QUORUM GLYPH IS OCCLUDED BY ITS OWN MAST, in the family's code and not this file's. _comp_quorum_one puts the mast at radius 0.035, z 0.065..0.135, y COMP_Y+0.00..+0.625, and the glyph ink plane at z COMP_Z + 0.03 = 0.130 with its centre at y COMP_Y + 0.455 = 0.600 and a line height of 20 * 0.005 = 0.10 m. The mast front is 5 mm nearer the camera than the ink and 0.070 m wide against a glyph about 0.045 m wide, so it covers all of it below y 0.625. Verbatim in f_order_bench.gd:343-358 and reproduced rather than repaired. It costs nothing: quorum is carried by the lit ring (33 px) and the mast (61 px), never by the tag.
  C-E. THE HEADER'S LAW 9 DAYLIGHTS ARE FLOORS, AND CONSERVATIVE ONES. It reports +11.4 / +27.9 / +12.5 px because it inflates the static part from AABB corners, which pairs extreme x with extreme z even where no mesh does. Projecting every actual mesh vertex at the widest variant of both axes gives +35.21 (A|B), +32.09 (B|C) and +25.32 (C|D) px at framing 0.44. All positive either way, and the binding gap is C|D, not A|B.
  C-F. "none|ghost BY THE SAME AMOUNT AT EACH VERDICT TO WITHIN 0.1 pp" IS RIGHT ABOUT THE KIT AND WRONG ABOUT THE NUMBER. The ghost kit's absolute changed area is verdict-independent to 0.6% (11,764 px at frozen and alive, 11,696 at noise) but the CROP is not: the union subject box is 728 x 350 at alive and noise and 728 x 251 at frozen, because bay C's column collapses and the box loses 99 rows. Same ink, smaller crop, bigger fraction: 0.9454% at alive against 1.3170% at frozen, a ratio of 1.3931 against the crop-area ratio of 1.3944. Agreement to 0.1%, and it is arithmetic, not an axis interaction.
  C-G. THE HEADER'S OWN FEAR ABOUT `ghost` DOES NOT SURVIVE THE RASTER. All four sources carry the same comment - grey and not black because "the capture stage is near-black, and a black value is an invisible one" - and the header predicts 6-12% focus, straddling TWIN_FOCUS 6.0%. Rasterised in the critic's currency the pair measures 18.19% focus, three times the twin bar. The worry was legitimate and the mount's grey is what answers it.
dna.kin:
`complement` IS TAKEN, NOT MINTED, and taken character for character (LAW 13): ["none", "ghost", "supply", "redaction", "quorum"], the list all four benches carry, in that order. Nothing added, nothing dropped, nothing renamed. This is the fifth token to carry the word and the first to carry four systems at once.

`verdict` IS ALSO TAKEN, from ONE bench, and the refusal is on the record. qfep_reactor_bench._verdict_state() returns "FROZEN", "NOISE" and "ALIVE"; those three strings are reused lowercased. lambda_dial_bench's "LIFE" IS REFUSED, because ALIVE occurs in two benches (the reactor's verdict state and phi_rate's "MOVING = ALIVE") and LIFE in one. TWO DIVERGENCES DECLARED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: (1) the ORDER is the court's, not the function's - _verdict_state is an if-ladder returning FROZEN, NOISE, ALIVE, and this axis runs frozen, alive, noise so that it is monotone in the sweep parameter s = 0.0, 0.5, 1.0; (2) f_order_bench prints no state word at all, so for bay A the word `verdict` is COINED BY THIS COURT and applied to a bench that never uses it. That is the finding, not an oversight - bay A's `frozen` cell is its own stated goal while the same cell is the other three benches' stated death - but it means the axis is not four-way shared the way `complement` is, and this entry does not claim it is.

WHAT `ghost` AND `none` MEAN HERE, WRITTEN SO THE OTHER FAMILY CAN BE HELD AGAINST IT WORD FOR WORD.

  NONE is a POSITION, not a neutral, and not a default. In all five files the `match complement` ends in a bare `pass` (ghost_court.gd:1010-1011, f_order:201-202, lambda_dial:202-203, phi_rate:188-189, reactor:209-210) with the same comment saying the dressing is appended LAST so that on `none` every child index above is untouched. Zero meshes, zero glyphs, and at `none` there is not one letter anywhere in the frame - the four bays stand unlabelled. What it means: each bench isolates one term of QFE = F - lambdaE(S) + phiDeltaE(S,t) and records NOTHING of the terms it dropped. f_order_bench.gd:31-35 states the cost: an instrument that isolates a variable is claiming something about what can be held still, and the claim is invisible precisely because nothing on the bench records it. For the reactor it is worse than silence - the bench is titled THE WHOLE FORMULA and carries a dial for F, lambda and phi while having no dial, pipe or mention of S, the system every term is a term OF. So NONE = ABSENCE UNMARKED.

  GHOST is PROVISION MADE AND NEVER FITTED. Per absent term: a capped stub post (0.05 radius, 0.30 tall), a torus collar sealing its top, a backing plate 0.23 x 0.27, a smaller BLANKED face plate 0.20 x 0.24 in darker grey, and the absent term's glyph engraved dead-grey on the blank. Every material is _matte_mat; nothing emits, nothing connects to the hub, nothing is lit. It is the socket the missing term would have been bolted into, capped, its face plate blank, its tag unlit. THREE THINGS IT IS NOT, and they are what makes the cross-family comparison sharp: it is not a DEPICTION of the absent term (there is no small lambda, no small phi, no miniature system); it is not a RESIDUE or afterimage of anything; and it is not a FORMER STATE of the phenomenon standing in the frame. The absent thing here is never the subject's own past - it is ANOTHER PARTY, another term of the equation the subject is one term of. GHOST = HARDWARE FOR A THIRD PARTY WHO NEVER ARRIVED.

  THE OTHER FAMILY, read but not owned by this pass. The `account` axis on the four translation cubes (axis_translation_cube.gd:80-95) declares [ghost, sweep, terminus, formula, none], where `ghost` is "four fading ghost cubes shrinking back along the path" - the moving object's OWN sampled former positions - and `none` is "the result only. A cube at a position, no rail, no markers, no ghosts". So the two families very nearly agree about `none` (both strip every companion apparatus and leave the bare phenomenon) and are OPPOSED about `ghost`: there it points backward in TIME at the same object, here it points sideways in the EQUATION at a different one. Both are "what is not here, drawn"; one is a history and one is a vacancy. [[passage_ledger]] owns that derivation and it must be checked against the code there rather than against this paragraph.
dna.declines:
EVERY RATE AND EVERY ANIMATION REFUSED (LAW 5), AND THIS IS THE HARDEST REFUSAL IN THE ENTRY because all four sources are animations. qfep_reactor_bench drives `_sweep` in _process, lambda_dial_bench drives `_lambda`, phi_rate_bench drives `_rate`, f_order_bench drives `_order`. ghost_court.gd has NO _process at all and calls set_process(false) at gd:500, and every source formula is evaluated at t = 0 in _unit_positions (gd:596-682). The `verdict` axis IS those live parameters, spatialised: three separate photographs at s = 0.0, 0.5, 1.0 (D_SWEEP), lambda = 0.0, 0.4, 1.0 (B_LAMBDA), order = 1.0, 0.5, 0.0 (A_ORDER), rate = 0.04, 1.0, 1.0 (C_RATE). A `speed` or `duration` axis would put the same information back into the time domain where a still cannot see it.

`term` REFUSED AS AN AXIS - which term each bench runs. It is already the BAY, drawn four times in one frame; promoting it would replace the comparison with a slideshow and delete the only thing this artifact can do that no single bench can.

`court_yaw`, `court_seed`, `court_gutter` and `court_ref_dist` ARE NOT AXES. They are rig constants and they are exported for maps and for reproducibility, not for sweeping. court_yaw is a placement knob (see spatial_needs.footprint_note) and sweeping it would re-frame every tile and re-base every pixel claim in this entry. court_seed is the LAW 6 pin: the court uses a deterministic hash of (index, draw, bay salt, seed) and NO RandomNumberGenerator anywhere, precisely so that a variant is never also a different scatter - all four sources call _rng.randomize(), and this file has no randf, no randi and no randomize.

`emissive` IS NOT AN AXIS. It is a plain `@export var emissive: bool = true` inherited from commons/artifacts/_embodied/embodied_prop.gd:8, gating _glow_mat and _steel_mat emission energy. A lighting gate, not declared in dna.axes, and it must not be swept.

A FIFTH BAY REFUSED. The obvious extension is a bay for the equation itself, or for the four benches' shared plinth vocabulary. It is refused on LAW 9: the binding daylight is already C|D at 25.32 px and a fifth bay at the same gutter pushes the rank past 6.6 m, which at the framing that keeps it in frame drops the ghost face plate from 30.7 px to about 25 px and bay D's particles from 4.09 to 3.3.

REPAIRING THE SOURCES REFUSED, THREE TIMES OVER, AND ALL THREE ARE VISIBLE IN THE FRAME. (1) phi_rate_bench.gd:194 + :212 double-add `column_center`, so bay C's column floats 1.07 m above the ring that emits it - reproduced, see dna.still_note R6. (2) The redaction bars strike terms that were never instantiated, so they redact blank bone - drawn as the code does it, not as the docstring says. (3) The quorum mast covers its own glyph (dna.note C-D). Only ONE source defect is repaired and it is declared: the reactor's readout screen spans z -0.1205..-0.1155 inside a panel spanning -0.130..-0.110 and has never been visible, and this court mounts it proud at -0.1085..-0.1035. The rule applied throughout is that a defect a still can SHOW is kept and a defect that makes a mesh invisible is fixed.
dna.framing_why:
CORRECTED FROM THE HEADER'S 0.39, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE WHOLE VALUE OF THIS PASS (dna.note C-A).

DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL 15 VARIANTS, computed by enumerating every mesh _build would create at all 5 x 3 combinations. The union is 5.1129 x 2.6617 x 4.0651 centred (0, 1.2608, 0), IDENTICAL AT EVERY VARIANT because the deck sets x and z alone and bay C's column sets y at two of the three verdicts. Diagonal 7.053443, radius 3.526722.

THE RIG: dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing = 3.526722 / 0.3057307 * 1.9 * 0.44 = 9.6436 m.

WHY 0.44 AND NOT 0.39. At 0.39 the camera stands at 8.548 m and the court projects to 822.7 px in a 760 px frame: it clips at both edges, the subject bbox comes back frame-clamped at x = 0..760, and bay A's and bay D's outer complement hardware - the mounts the closest pair is made of - fall off the picture. At 0.44 the projected span is 16.28..743.72 px, 727.4 px = 95.7% of frame width, with 16 px of margin either side. At framing 1.0 the rig fits by bounding SPHERE and a 5.38 m rank would fill 36% of frame width, which is the documented wide-flat failure mode and would put the ghost face plate at 13 px and bay D's particles at 1.8 px.

AND 0.44 IS NOT A NEW SOLUTION, IT IS THE HEADER'S OWN. Eight independent figures the header quotes reproduce at 0.44 and at no other value, which is what identifies its 0.39 as a typo rather than a different design:

  header                              replica at framing 0.44
  128.9 px/m                          128.89 px/m at the subject plane
  "96% of frame width"                95.7%, span 16.28..743.72 px
  ghost face plate 25.8 x 30.9 px     25.56 x 30.67
  ghost backing 29.7 x 34.8 px        29.39 x 34.50
  ghost capped post 12.9 x 38.7 px    12.78 x 38.34
  supply riser 7.2 x 36.1 px          7.16 x 35.78
  quorum ring OD 33.3 px              32.97
  quorum needle 1.8 x 11.0 px         1.79 x 10.86
  bay D particle 4.1 px               4.09

(The small residual is that the header quotes the subject-plane scale of 128.9 px/m and the replica quotes each mark at its own bay's depth; the worst bay is A/B/C at 127.80 px/m.)

LAW 8: THE GAUGE IS PER BAY, AND THIS IS THE RANK WHERE THE ANSWER IS ONE NUMBER HONESTLY. The camera direction in court-local components is (0, 0.25708, 0.96634) and the screen-right vector is (1, 0, 0), so court-local x IS screen-x and a rank laid along it sits at ONE depth.
